submission.natural_language_explanation: L5/H5 turns an open-class anchor into a predicate-verb prior: it attends almost one-hot (weight 1.0 in 18 of 20 top examples, at the current token or the last content word before it) and writes that token's layer-5 value, whose logit lens is exactly the set of verbs that can follow it (indicate, show, reveal, suggest, demonstrate, have), and mean-ablating the head costs those verbs plus the copulas that follow a subject ('are', 'were', 'is', 'suggest', 'show', 'indicate', 'have'; KL 0.05, spread over many verb forms, which is why the protocol's concentration test reads the mechanism as retrospective rather than lookahead). Strength is how far that write sits from the head's mean write: 2.6-3.6 for abstract, usually plural deverbal nominals (findings, observations, results, pressures, experiments, estimates, studies, warnings, comments, differences), 1.2-2.3 for concrete count nouns and finite verbs (cats, bottles, tables, slept, failed), near the median (0.0-0.3) for function words in running prose and for the sequence's first token, which it attends when nothing else matches, and a strong anchor's value is re-written at later nominals of its phrase ('The results of the study of the trial' reads 2.9 at all three nouns), so a text is inactive when it offers no open-class anchor at all - a single token, one frequent token repeated, or a digit/number run (0.0-0.5, at any length) - while short generic clauses are borderline ('The chair was clear.' 0.9, 'The dog was clear.' 1.2) and closed-class strings, symbol runs, non-Latin script and code cross at whichever fragment token spikes.
rival_explanations: Narrower nominalization detector: the head tracks abstract deverbal plural nouns specifically, so it predicts that concrete count nouns (bottles, chairs, cats, tables), singular nouns and finite verbs stay below the line and only nominalizations like findings, studies and estimates cross it.

Context-free token-anomaly detector: the head fires on whatever token is unusual in itself - rare fragments, symbol runs, repeated rare words, non-Latin glyphs, function-word lists - predicting that 'studies' alone fires as strongly as 'studies' inside a clause and that concrete nouns fire as strongly as abstract ones when equally rare.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At the close of the third quarter the compliance office circulated a short memorandum to every regional manager. It described the new filing requirements, the revised timetable for submissions, the penalties for late disclosure, and the procedure for appealing a rejection. Only at the end did it set out, in unusually plain language, the observations that had come out of the spring inspections, together with a list of deadlines and the names of the two firms whose records had been seized. The memorandum asked managers to reply within ten working days and to copy their answers to the general counsel, who would report the results to the board in November.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis predicts a strong write (2.6-3.6) at the intact anchor tokens ' observations' and ' results' late in a long ordinary prose passage, a genre and position absent from the examples.

One unbroken digit string is the hardest form of the number run the hypothesis says reads 0.0-0.5 at any length, even though its fragments recur.
Halving decimals are rare numeric fragments, yet the hypothesis's number-run class still predicts 0.0-0.5 and no activity.
A long measurement list matches the longest holdout in length while staying a pure number run of digit and '.' tokens, which the hypothesis says is inactive at any length.
